tutorial:
(In VR mode, please press B to go next, and press A to go previous.
In non-VR mode, please press Enter to go next, Backspace to go previous)
This is my notebook of prior experiences flying with Toothless.
I designed a pedal-controlled tail wing to guide our direction of flight.
The right pedal controls yaw.
(In VR mode, the right joystick turns left and right)
(In non-VR mode, the ← and → arrow keys turn left and right)
I think I need more practice with these basic maneuvers.
/!1(Please turn to the next page if you think you've finished this phase of practice)
The left pedal controls pitch.
(In VR mode, the left joystick controls looking up and down)
(In non-VR mode, the ↑ and ↓ arrow keys control looking up and down)
If I pull up, we decelerate. Conversely, if I dive, we gain noticeable speed.
Toothless flaps his wings to maintain speed, so I don't need to worry about stalling.
/!1(Please turn to the next page if you think you've finished this phase of practice)
In a crisis, we both tense up, and Toothless responds to my actions very quickly. (In VR mode, please tilt your head sideways to control yaw)
At first it was hard to control this behavior, but with practice I found we could perform fairly delicate maneuvers.
/!2(Please turn to the next page if you think you've finished this phase of practice)
From my observations, some birds roll upside down to descend quickly in flight to avoid predators.
This redirects the lift generated by the wings downward, allowing them to accelerate toward the ground faster than free fall.
I found that Toothless knows this move as well. (In VR mode, press the Y button; in non-VR mode, press the space bar)
We can use this tactic to quickly lose altitude during flight to avoid obstacles ahead or above.
/!2(Please turn to the next page if you think you've finished this phase of practice)
That went pretty well. I think now I should take a look at the place for the test drive. (In VR mode, press Y button; in non-VR mode, press Esc key to bring up the return menu)
